races.name: Sky Bet Lowther Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Alta Regina
runners_data.note: Won a 5f maiden on Good ground but steps up sharply in class here; a natural pace-lover who won't get her habitual spot so easily with Libertango, Livenka and Moonrise already filling those premium slots, diluting her chance meaningfully.

runners_data.name: Angels Passing
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won over this exact C&D on Good ground last time — the 77-day break is a concern, but Kevin Stott is likely to send her straight to the front and she'll test every rival for stamina.

runners_data.name: Big Negotiator
runners_data.note: Top-rated among the front-runners at OR 102, wears a visor, and has six starts on Good ground including two wins — strong claims to lead the way, though facing three-way pace competition makes holding a clean early lead far from certain.

runners_data.name: Bint Archange
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the mount on this confirmed front-runner who has won twice on Good ground over 5f — stepping up to 6f for the first time is a genuine question mark, and the pace battle with Big Negotiator and Angels Passing may cost her dearly in the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Crownbreaker
runners_data.note: Prominent type with solid form at 5f on Good ground but hasn't won over this trip; David Egan will need to find a clean passage in a very busy prominent group and the step to 6f on Good going is untested for this filly.

runners_data.name: Crystal Queen
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer who won a Goodwood 5f maiden on Good ground; Connor Beasley will likely sit last or near-last, making her entirely dependent on pace collapse and a clear run — the scenario is plausible but requires things to go her way.

runners_data.name: Desert Sands
runners_data.note: OR 75 makes this the lowest-rated runner in the field; a natural prominent type who has been redistributed to the rear because hold-up slots needed filling, so she'll likely be out of her comfort zone positionally and faces a steep class rise.

runners_data.name: In The Black
runners_data.note: Won her only start impressively over 5f on Good ground but is lightly raced and an unknown quantity stepping into Group 2 company; Geoff Oldroyd's sole representative, she'll emerge from well off the pace having been mapped there by default — her raw ability is intriguing but unexposed.

runners_data.name: Jolivette
runners_data.note: William Buick rides a filly who won her maiden over this exact 6f Good course convincingly; a natural pace-seeker who won't easily secure her preferred position in this traffic-heavy field, which blunts her chance compared to a less congested race.

runners_data.name: Libertango
runners_data.note: Two wins from three over 6f on Good ground, including a Listed success; Billy Loughnane on a horse perfectly suited to racing prominently at genuine pace — rates among the most likely winners if she slots into a clean position just off the lead.

runners_data.name: Livenka
runners_data.note: Four starts, two wins, all on Good ground over 6f-7f for GM Lyons — Colin Keane's positive booking is significant and she arrives in the form of her life having won twice on the bounce; well-equipped for a truly-run race.

runners_data.name: Love A Giggle
runners_data.note: Won twice at 5f and was placed in a good 6f nursery — a natural pace-seeker who is unlikely to get her habitual forward berth in this traffic-heavy field, so Clifford Lee will need to adapt his tactics and the filly may not be seen to best effect.

runners_data.name: Miss Kodi
runners_data.note: Won her sole start over 6f on Soft ground but has a Good-ground win only at 5f; Rossa Ryan faces the problem that this filly wants to race prominently but there are simply too many rivals with equal or stronger claims to that position.

runners_data.name: Moonrise
runners_data.note: Two wins over 6f on Good ground and placed in a Listed race — Oisin Murphy on a consistent, well-rounded filly who should handle the prominent spot well; a strong place candidate in the most likely race shape with further upside if she gets a clear run.

runners_data.name: Ruby Moon
runners_data.note: Won her maiden over 6f on Good ground at the Fahey yard; Oisin Orr will want to race prominently, and while she's competitive at this level, she faces stronger market rivals who have more established Group-race credentials.

runners_data.name: Sexy Chick
runners_data.note: Won a Newmarket 6f maiden on Good ground and shaped nicely when second; a pace-loving type who is squeezed out of her preferred position by the sheer volume of prominent horses here, meaning George Wood will likely have to improvise tactically.

runners_data.name: Shimmering Sun
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand rides a filly who won at 5f on Good ground and finished second in a solid 5f event — the step to 6f is untested on Good, but Harry Eustace's operation is in solid form and she could outrun market expectations if the pace is strong.

runners_data.name: Star Of State
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's highest-profile runner at OR 120 — Dylan Browne McMonagle takes over and this filly has won and placed over 6f on Good ground; the class benchmark in the prominent group and must be respected if she gets a clean position.

runners_data.name: Wild Blossom
runners_data.note: Two wins from three over 5f on Good ground for KR Burke — James Doyle will play it positively from a prominent position and the step to 6f on Good ground looks within range; a lively each-way contender if the pace is honest.

races.paceDynamic: Big Negotiator, Bint Archange and Angels Passing are all confirmed front-runners and will compete aggressively for the lead from the gates, guaranteeing a strong, unrelenting gallop over York's straight 6f. With eight of the 19 runners wanting prominent positions, there will be fierce early scrapping for territory, creating significant traffic danger between the 2f and 3f markers as horses bunch and jostle. This pace-dominated shape will stretch the field, burning off those who expend excessive energy early and leaving the race to be decided by the strongest stayers in the final furlong — a profile that heavily favours runners who can sit just off the speed in a genuine rhythm and unleash a sustained finish rather than a sprint burst. This field carries far more pace than the map can accommodate: Alta Regina, Jolivette, Miss Kodi, Love A Giggle and Sexy Chick are natural prominent runners who will not all secure their preferred position, with Libertango, Livenka, Star Of State and Moonrise — the classier, more settled prominent types — best placed to actually hold those crucial slots just behind the contested lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hot Pace, Prominent Sweep
scenarios.trigger: If Big Negotiator and Bint Archange burn each other off at a genuine Group 2 gallop, the race falls to a high-class horse racing prominently but under restraint.
scenarios.body: The three front-runners take each other on through a blistering first 3f, and the winner emerges from the prominent group just off the pace, benefiting from a clear run and the strong tempo to power home in the final furlong. Libertango, Livenka, Star Of State and Moonrise all profile perfectly for this shape — each has a track record of winning off genuine pace on Good ground over 6f.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Big Negotiator Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Big Negotiator asserts early dominance and the other front-runners fail to sustain their challenge, he could control a tactical contest from the front.
scenarios.body: Big Negotiator has the highest OR of the three leaders, has a visor on, and has the class to dictate if Bint Archange and Angels Passing drop away — an uncontested lead over Good ground at York would suit his profile admirably. Horses who can track him at a steadier pace and quicken in the final 2f would threaten, but his class and experience give him every chance to convert.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the prominently-congested field causes significant interference between the 2f and 3f poles, horses switched outside late from midfield could benefit.
scenarios.body: The congestion of eight horses chasing prominent spots creates a realistic scenario where several stumble in traffic, leaving a clear passage on the outside for runners like Crystal Queen who are comfortable coming from behind. True hold-up types and redistributed midfielders are limited in this race, so the actual beneficiaries would need to be legitimately patient runners; Crystal Queen fits best, but the scenario is constrained by the scarcity of genuine closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Angels Passing or Bint Archange breaks sharply and the other confirmed leaders miss the start or are checked, a lone front-runner could steal the race at a more manageable gallop.
scenarios.body: This shape requires at least two of the three front-runners to fail to assert, a low-probability outcome given their established styles, but if it materialises the beneficiary would dictate from the front and exploit the field's disorganisation in chasing. Angels Passing won over this C&D last time out on Good ground and would be the primary candidate to steal it if such a scenario unfolds.

watchPoints.text: Big Negotiator, Bint Archange and Angels Passing will fight for the lead from the gates — watch for a chaotic opening furlong where any one of them could be bumped, checked or forced wide, fundamentally altering the race shape.

The prominent group of eight runners jostling for five or six positions between 2f and 3f out represents a serious traffic hazard — Jolivette, Miss Kodi, Love A Giggle and Alta Regina are all at elevated risk of being blocked or forced to check at a critical moment.

Bint Archange is unproven over 6f having run exclusively at 5f — if Ryan Moore is forced to commit hard early to secure the lead against Big Negotiator, the extra furlong may expose her stamina limitations in the final 100 yards.

In The Black's single start (a 5f win) leaves her form deeply exposed at Group 2 level — PJ McDonald will be riding a largely unknown quantity and the horse's best position in the map is a redistribution artefact rather than a confident tactical read.

Star Of State carries the joint-top OR of 120 alongside In The Black — Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking from the powerful O'Brien stable is a strong positive flag and warrants monitoring in the market as a market mover.

races.name: Harry's Half Million By Goffs (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Tokaido
runners_data.note: Five wins from six including a hat-trick, trained by Amy Murphy with Tony Piccone aboard; a prominent racer blessed with a high OR of 120 and rock-solid Good-going record, but facing the stiffest competition of his career in a race where holding prominent position will be genuinely difficult with this pace.

runners_data.name: Furturra
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's consistent two-year-old has won twice and placed six times from ten runs with an excellent record at Good; naturally wants to race prominently but this field has too many genuine pace horses ahead of him, meaning he is very likely to race further back than his style dictates — temper expectations accordingly.

runners_data.name: Mind Those Steps
runners_data.note: David Allan's mount wears a hood and has been freshened up at 26 days since last run; a hold-up horse whose single York win came at exactly this trip and going, making the course form a genuine asset if the front runners burn each other out.

runners_data.name: Where Love Lives
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane takes a high-profile booking for Donnacha Aidan O'Brien's raider, who has two wins from four runs with a solid Good-going strike rate; a hold-up operator who wants a strong pace to close into, and this race provides exactly that scenario — primary beneficiary of the anticipated meltdown.

runners_data.name: The Bookkeeper
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes' runner arrives on the back of a seven-furlong run at Good that will have sharpened him; a prominent-style horse stepping back in trip whose patchy recent form and single Good-going placing gives limited confidence in a race this competitive.

runners_data.name: Sun Goddess
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partners the highest-profile confirmed pace horse in the race, with three wins from five starts all at Good going and a recent York victory; the danger is that Secret Society and Satellite Of Love force her into a costly duel from flag fall, but Moore's tactical intelligence gives her every chance to find a clear lead cheaply if rivals interfere with each other.

runners_data.name: Battle Fever
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's two-year-old is unbeaten in three, all at Good, giving him a perfect going record; however, his natural prominent style cannot be fulfilled here — he will be pushed into a role he has never raced from before, which significantly mutes his chance regardless of his ability.

runners_data.name: Blake's Monarch
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's runner has been off 61 days and finished tenth on Good going last time, with only one placing from three starts; a confirmed leader who will likely be swallowed up in the pack of pace horses disputing supremacy.

runners_data.name: Glorious Game
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's runner has won twice from three starts including a York win at this trip on Good, but finished ninth on the same track last time; drops back in form concern but Oisin Murphy's presence adds tactical intrigue — a confirmed leader who needs to find daylight in a very competitive pace group.

runners_data.name: Innichen
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand partners a horse with two wins from five on Good going, most recently a solid third in a six-furlong York handicap; a prominent racer who has actually fulfilled his style in similar races before and whose recent form is consistent enough to be competitive if he can secure his position.

runners_data.name: It Dunt Marra
runners_data.note: Stevie Donohoe's mount has won at Good going at five furlongs and is stepping up in trip for the first time; a prominent racer whose chance rests on whether he can handle the six-furlong distance and the increased field size, with modest OR of 82 limiting expectations.

runners_data.name: Kodiak Breeze
runners_data.note: Two wins from three starts all at Good, trained by Kevin Ryan who also runs Battle Fever; a confirmed leader racing back to six furlongs where he has won, and with the best going record in the confirmed pace group — better placed than some rivals to sustain the pace if the battle for the lead is quickly settled.

runners_data.name: Pride Of Toledo
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's highest-rated prospect in the race alongside Secret Society at OR 120, with Callum Rodriguez aboard; a prominent racer who won last time over this exact trip and going and is lightly raced enough to still be improving — well positioned to benefit if he can sit just off the lead pack.

runners_data.name: Quillan
runners_data.note: Kaiya Fraser partners a two-from-two winner, both at Good, stepping up significantly in class from five furlongs; a confirmed leader facing her sternest test yet, and the class jump combined with the fierce pace battle means her unbeaten record is under real threat.

runners_data.name: Satellite Of Love
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan's mount is two from two for Clive Cox, both wins at York over six furlongs on Good — an exact course, distance, and going match; a confirmed leader who must fight for the early lead against five or six rivals, though her perfect record at this track gives her a fighting chance of securing it.

runners_data.name: Secret Society
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle partners Clive Cox's third runner in the race, but form of 3-6 is the least impressive of the confirmed pace horses; finished sixth on soft and third on Good — going is no concern but recent form is exposed and she may find herself in an energy-sapping duel with superior pace horses.

runners_data.name: Thebesthasyetocome
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley's Irish raider has been off 61 days and has only one win from two starts on Good going over five furlongs; the step up to six is untested and the long absence adds risk, though the win form is solid enough to justify a fringe interest.

runners_data.name: Weekend Roar
runners_data.note: James Doyle takes a quality booking for Hugo Palmer's runner, who won over this trip on Good going last time and finished third at the same track; a prominent racer with a clean recent record who represents a credible each-way profile if the pace creates gaps in the straight.

runners_data.name: Niewiadoma
runners_data.note: Gina Mangan's mount wore a hood and finished 17th, 25th, and 9th in her last three starts after winning on debut, showing a clear fade pattern in finishes ⚠; a hold-up horse who has conspicuously lost her way in form and looks very hard to recommend despite the going posing no concern.

runners_data.name: Rollthedicebaby
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's two-year-old has Sean Levey in the saddle and has placed at Good going but finished sixth last time; a genuinely prominent-type racer pushed into a midfield mapping because the field is saturated with pace horses — his best form comes when racing up with the pace which he is unlikely to be able to do here.

runners_data.name: Speed of Sound
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne's mount has won most recently over this exact trip and going, progressive across three runs at six furlongs; a prominent racer whose freshness at 15 days since last run and improving profile makes her a live outside contender if she can find a clear run from her natural position.

runners_data.name: Vollering
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's runner wears a hood and has been tried at five and six furlongs on Good and Soft, finishing placed four times without a win since her debut; a prominent racer whose consistency is clear but whose lack of a win since debut and moderate OR of 96 suggests she is a frame horse rather than a winner in this company.

races.paceDynamic: Sun Goddess, Secret Society, Satellite Of Love, Blake's Monarch, Glorious Game, Kodiak Breeze, and Quillan all want to lead, creating a genuinely fierce pace battle from the stalls in a wide-open 22-runner field over six furlongs at York. With six or seven horses disputing the early lead, the gallop will be strong and unrelenting from the outset, compressing the field and making it very hard for the pace-setters to conserve energy for the final furlong. Tokaido, Pride Of Toledo, and Innichen among the prominent types will face intense congestion two to three furlongs out, where nine runners are chasing the same ground in a narrow corridor. This race shape strongly favours hold-up or late-midfield runners who can settle behind the carnage and pick up the pieces — Where Love Lives, Mind Those Steps, and Speed of Sound represent the profile that benefits most from this unsustainable pace. The field contains more genuine prominent and front-running types than the race can accommodate — Furturra, Battle Fever, and Rollthedicebaby are true prominent racers who are unlikely to secure their natural position in this shape and should be treated with caution accordingly; Secret Society, Sun Goddess, and Satellite Of Love — as confirmed leaders — are most likely to actually secure the early rail positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Reign
scenarios.trigger: If the six-plus pace horses burn each other out inside two furlongs, creating a strong-pace meltdown that sets the race up for those racing off the tempo.
scenarios.body: The frenetic early pace will see the leaders hit the wall turning for home, leaving the field strung out and fatigued in the final furlong; hold-up and midfield types racing on fresh legs will sweep past the exhausted leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Sits, Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If one prominent runner manages to settle just off the scorching pace and quickens decisively when the leaders tie up.
scenarios.body: A horse like Tokaido or Pride Of Toledo, who has the class to sit a length or two off the leaders in a race where the true front-runners are fighting each other, can time a run to the line as rivals compound; the high OR ratings and strong recent form of this pair makes them the most credible beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the confirmed pace horses — specifically Sun Goddess — manages to steal a break, find a clear lead, and control the pace sufficiently to hold on.
scenarios.body: Sun Goddess has five runs at Good going, has won three of them on this course and distance, and is partnered by Ryan Moore, who can judge a pace better than most in a field of rivals likely to interfere with each other; if she settles fractionally cleaner than her rivals and establishes daylight quickly, her class gives her a genuine chance to last home.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos Produces Upset
scenarios.trigger: If traffic trouble two to three furlongs out scrambles the market leaders and a lightly-raced, unexposed runner emerges from the pack to score.
scenarios.body: With 22 runners and nine horses chasing prominent ground simultaneously, interference and checking is a realistic outcome that can bring a runner like Speed of Sound or It Dunt Marra to prominence at a price; horses with clean recent form, modest weights, and the ability to find daylight on the outside of the pack could exploit the scramble.

watchPoints.text: Sun Goddess and Satellite Of Love are confirmed leaders trained by the same handler (Clive Cox) — watch whether one effectively acts as pacemaker for the other, which could give one a decisive tactical advantage over the rest of the pace group.

Where Love Lives arrives as a hold-up horse perfectly suited to a strong pace, but with 22 runners over six furlongs at York, Billy Loughnane will need a clear run from two furlongs out — any traffic trouble in the pack could cost her dearly despite a winning profile.

Secret Society, Blake's Monarch, and Glorious Game are all confirmed leaders but arrive with patchy or declining recent form — watch whether any of these cause an unnecessarily frantic early pace before weakening, compounding the carnage for closers.

Battle Fever, Furturra, and Rollthedicebaby are all natural prominent types who cannot get their position in this race — if any of them are switched to hold-up tactics by their jockeys in-race, they are effectively racing completely out of their comfort zone and should be discounted even if they appear on the speed map.

Tokaido has five wins from six with a dominant recent profile but faces his first truly competitive elite field — Tony Piccone must judge whether to push for his natural prominent berth or settle and risk losing ground; the tactical decision made in the first furlong will define his race.

races.name: Sir Kevin Sinfield 7 In 7 Grand Finale Handicap Stakes (Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Point Lynas
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent performer at this course (six 8f runs here), trainer Bethell in fine form at 9/24, but a disappointing recent run of 67-942 suggests he is not at his best and a wide draw could force him early into traffic in a congested prominent group.

runners_data.name: Arctic Dawn
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good recently and trainer Kubler sends him here sharp at 12 days; he races prominently but all five listed runs are over 7f — this step up to a mile is a key stamina question and he may force the early pace rather than settle.

runners_data.name: Cerulean Bay
runners_data.note: Tudhope on this David O'Meara stable regular who has 13 of 15 runs on Good ground; placed at 8f here twice and a reliable prominent racer, though the 258429 form string suggests a horse just outside the frame rather than winning.

runners_data.name: Centigrade
runners_data.note: The only genuine front-runner in the field — Ralph Beckett sends him here after a 63-day break, but his form reads 21/1 (two wins including one at 8f on Standard) and he can control this entirely; the sole leader in a 17-runner field is a significant tactical weapon.

runners_data.name: The Lost King
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride for Andrew Balding (6/49 in 14 days) — a horse who has won over this exact course and distance and ran creditably at 9f; prominent style, genuine Good-ground form, and a top jockey booking signal serious intent.

runners_data.name: Bullet Point
runners_data.note: William Haggas runner at 131lbs for Tom Marquand, returned 12 days ago; placed at this trip on Good ground but the 70-702 recent form suggests he finds one or two too good, and a prominent pitch in a busy field makes clean passage uncertain.

runners_data.name: Checkandchallenge
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with zero wins from 15 Good-ground runs but four places; raced here over 8f three times placing once — his consistency without a win is the recurring theme, though a muddled race with traffic could present a late opportunity.

runners_data.name: Blue Brother
runners_data.note: James Doyle partner, but the /60-48 form is unimpressive and no wins recorded on Good — he races prominently, making the early congestion potentially costly, and his trainer T14 of just 1/3 suggests limited current yard form.

runners_data.name: Eternal Force
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle rides this William Haggas four-year-old off a 56-day break; blinkered (hg:b), won twice on Soft but also placed at 8f on Good — the blinkers and top jockey hint at a freshened-up yard hope, though his best form came on softer ground.

runners_data.name: Mezcala
runners_data.note: William Buick and a horse who won over 7f on Good and placed at 8f on Good; a hold-up performer who is dropped back in distance after a 9f attempt, and Buick's ability to find a late passage gives this runner genuine tactical appeal if the race is run to suit closers.

runners_data.name: Hawksbill
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with 13 of 15 runs on Good but no wins from those races; all recent runs over 7f mean this step to 8f is a slight question, and a modest OR of 93 makes it difficult to win a Heritage Handicap off this mark without a career-best effort.

runners_data.name: Mirsky
runners_data.note: David O'Meara stable companion to Cerulean Bay — form reads 100799 and he is tagged as fading in the finish; a natural front-runner or prominent racer who will be shuffled into the midfield pack by the sheer weight of forward-going horses, negating his most effective running position entirely.

runners_data.name: Nizam
runners_data.note: Clifford Lee partner for Ian Williams returning after 63 days — the 56-070 recent form is concerning, and 3 of 10 Good-ground runs have placed, suggesting inconsistency; the extended layoff combined with uninspiring recent form makes this a risky proposition in a competitive Heritage field.

runners_data.name: Yorkshire
runners_data.note: Bethell's second runner alongside Point Lynas, PJ McDonald up; the 9-0923 form includes a third over 8f on Good recently, but like Mirsky he is a genuine prominent type who will find his preferred position squeezed out, and his headgear note (hg:t) suggests he needs to be covered up anyway.

runners_data.name: Aalto
runners_data.note: Ian Williams three-runner handler — Saffie Osborne takes this hold-up performer who won over 7f on Good 26 days ago and was placed twice; a step to 8f should suit a horse who has 11 of 15 runs on Good, and the trajectory of his form (213 recently) is encouraging.

runners_data.name: Spell Master
runners_data.note: Oli Rix four-year-old with 1 win and mixed handicap form at 7-9f; naturally a prominent racer but will be displaced into midfield by the prominent crowd — his best run was a 7f win on Standard track, and Good 8f at York in a 17-runner Heritage Handicap is a significant ask.

runners_data.name: The Angel King
runners_data.note: Ian Williams completes a three-runner stable team — Edward Greatrex rides a hold-up horse who has been placed over 7f on Good; the redistribution note means he ends up in a midfield position not far from his natural style anyway, but his OR of 89 is near the bottom of this field.

races.paceDynamic: Centigrade is the sole confirmed front-runner and, on Good ground at York over a mile, is expected to bowl along at a sustainable but not suicidal gallop — with no genuine rival for the lead, Rossa Ryan can dictate terms entirely on his own terms. Behind him, however, there is a congested battle for the prominent positions: Point Lynas, Arctic Dawn, Cerulean Bay, The Lost King, Bullet Point, Blue Brother, and Eternal Force all want to race in the first four or five, creating near-certain scrimmaging and traffic interference from the two-furlong pole inward. The field holds more prominent types than can all get their natural position — Mirsky, Yorkshire, and Spell Master are genuine forward racers who will be shuffled back into an unnatural midfield slot, undermining their effectiveness. This race shape — a controlled, uncontested gallop set by a single leader — classically favours horses who can sit just off the pace in a clean position and produce a sustained, well-timed run, meaning true-prominent horses who avoid the early traffic and patient hold-up performers with a turn of foot are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Centigrade Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Centigrade leads at a measured gallop and the prominent horses directly behind him get clean early runs.
scenarios.body: Centigrade sets a comfortable tempo, allowing horses settled just off the pace in positions two through five to travel within themselves and strike decisively from two furlongs out without needing to find gaps; the moderate pace means the race is run to suit those who can quicken off a sound but unspectacular gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Late Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent logjam causes persistent interference and the race is truly run for stamina from the front.
scenarios.body: The scramble for the early prominent positions forces several horses wide or into tight pockets approaching the straight, burning energy and leaving the door open for the hold-up horses who have bypassed the chaos on the outside; William Buick on Mezcala and a freshened Checkandchallenge become the chief beneficiaries as the race develops into a true test of resolution.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Fast Early Pace, Front Runner Fades
scenarios.trigger: If pressure from the prominent group forces Centigrade into an unsustainably quick early gallop that cuts the race up.
scenarios.body: Should multiple prominent horses push up hard in the early stages — Arctic Dawn or Blue Brother refusing to settle — the pace accelerates and Centigrade is compromised, leaving the race wide open for a closer with a high cruising speed to reel them in; Eternal Force, who has won on soft ground and has a high cruising speed, and The Lost King both possess the class to capitalise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Centigrade Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If Centigrade is left completely alone, slips the field entering the straight, and the prominent pack is too congested to respond.
scenarios.body: With no rival pushing him, Rossa Ryan steals a decisive advantage down the back before the prominent horses have resolved their positional battle, and the gaps simply never materialise for those held up; Centigrade's recent course-and-distance form (two wins on similar surfaces) makes this an underappreciated threat if the tactical scenario unfolds cleanly.

watchPoints.text: Watch the first two furlongs closely — with seven horses wanting prominent positions and only Centigrade genuinely holding the lead role, Arctic Dawn, Blue Brother, and Bullet Point are all likely to press forward aggressively and create a bunching incident that could trap several runners on the rail entering the back straight.

Mirsky, Yorkshire, and Spell Master are all natural prominent types who will be squeezed back into the midfield — if any of them fight for position in the first half-mile, they will burn energy and be spent before the straight, making them false pointers for pace handicappers tracking their early movements.

Centigrade's 63-day absence is the key unknown — if Ralph Beckett has him tuned up this is a significant advantage for a lone front-runner, but if he shows any rustiness or is allowed to coast at a falsely slow pace, the race could compress dramatically entering the final two furlongs and produce a chaotic finish.

William Buick on Mezcala and Oisin Murphy on The Lost King are the two standout jockey bookings for horses whose styles genuinely suit the expected race shape — monitor their positioning at the top of the straight, as both riders will look to find a clear run down the outside if the inner is blocked.

York's mile on Good ground typically rewards horses settled within three lengths of the leader at the two-furlong pole — any horse more than five lengths adrift at that point faces a steep task given the flat, unrelenting nature of the York straight and the likely modest early gallop set by a single leader.

races.name: Legends Global Yorkshire Oaks (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Kalpana
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's in-form five-year-old arrives on the back of consecutive 1m2f wins on Good ground and steps up in trip here, a move that her pedigree and sustained finishing efforts strongly support; she races prominently and is tactically versatile enough to slot just behind the pace battle and exploit any leaders who overdo it.

runners_data.name: Minnie Hauk
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride for A P O'Brien on this four-year-old who has mixed form over 1m2f on Good ground but whose sole win at 1m4f looks relevant here; she has tended to race prominently but can be covered up, and Moore's ability to find the right position in a pace-heavy race is a clear tactical advantage.

runners_data.name: Tattycoram
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's mare has won her last two starts over 1m2f on Good ground at this very track and has the profile of a horse who improves sharply with front-running tactics; Edward Greatrex partners her and must commit early to secure the lead against Johanna Walsh, making the first two furlongs a critical battleground.

runners_data.name: Earth Shot
runners_data.note: William Haggas's three-year-old is a natural prominent racer in terms of how she prefers to be ridden — she has won off front-rank positions before — but with the front-running slots already fiercely contested she is likely to end up in a chasing prominent role rather than dictating; James Doyle will need to find cover and hope the pace scenario produces a fast-finishing opportunity.

runners_data.name: Inis Mor
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's three-year-old for David Menuisier showed a career-best when winning over 1m2f on Good ground and stays 1m4f adequately based on her placed effort; she races prominently and could sit just off the likely pace battle, giving Murphy a platform to challenge if the leaders soften each other up.

runners_data.name: Johanna Walsh
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle rides this Joseph O'Brien-trained filly who has proven front-running credentials and is effective with the headgear flag noted; she won over 1m2f on Good ground and will need to assert herself immediately against Tattycoram to avoid being crowded out, but her jockey is among the most aggressive and talented at making the running.

runners_data.name: Legacy Link
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's three-year-old has been off 63 days which is the longest absence in this field, and William Buick must weigh up a horse who has shown front-running ability but whose form over 1m4f on Good ground is still developing; she may be unable to force the pace if Johanna Walsh and Tattycoram are determined, sliding her into a prominent-chasing role by default.

runners_data.name: Sparan Nua
runners_data.note: Jim Bolger's three-year-old has had a busy campaign, running just 14 days ago, and has won three of her five starts on Good ground including back-to-back victories; Rossa Ryan will likely position her prominently given her natural inclination, but the elevated pace of this race is a stamina test she has not yet definitively answered at 1m4f.

runners_data.name: Sugar Island
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien's second string on OR=102, Sugar Island has struggled in her last three starts at 1m2f on Good ground and her form string reveals a sharp dip in class competitiveness; Ronan Whelan will likely try to get her into a prominent position but the quality of the front-running contingent here makes that difficult, and she enters as the most significant vulnerability in the field.

races.paceDynamic: Three confirmed front-runners — Johanna Walsh, Tattycoram, and Legacy Link — alongside prominent-pressing Sugar Island ensure this 1m4f Group 1 will be run at a genuine, unrelenting gallop from the outset on Good ground at York. Tattycoram and Johanna Walsh are both natural leaders who will not concede the rail cheaply, with Legacy Link and Sugar Island adding further pressure through the first half of the race, meaning no runner will get an easy lead and the pace is likely to remain honest rather than suicidal but firmly competitive throughout. The result is a race that will stretch stamina reserves and compress the finishing kick, meaning the premium will be on horses who can travel strongly in behind, make smooth progress into the straight, and sustain their effort over York's stiff uphill finish — a profile that classically rewards the well-positioned, resolute galloper over the pure speedster. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can realistically all get their position; of those, Johanna Walsh with her proven ability to dominate from the front, and Tattycoram with recent winning form over this course and distance, are most likely to actually secure the early lead, while Legacy Link and Sparan Nua are more likely to be shuffled into a prominent-chasing role rather than dictating.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Stamina Verdict
scenarios.trigger: If Johanna Walsh and Tattycoram fight for early supremacy and sustain a genuine gallop that tests every runner's stamina from the 5f pole.
scenarios.body: The front two set an unrelenting tempo that shreds the field turning for home, leaving only those with deep reserves able to peg them back; prominent hold-up racers with proven 1m4f stamina are perfectly positioned to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Johanna Walsh or Tattycoram secures a clear, uncontested lead and dictates a controlled gallop that suits their strengths.
scenarios.body: One front-runner gets away from the others early and settles into a rhythm that draws the sting from rivals before kicking clear in the straight; York's galloping track rewards those who can dictate and sustain without being pushed into overdoing it.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Class Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fierce enough to cause the leaders to tie up inside the final furlong and a prominent tracker delivers a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: A strong early gallop burns off the front-runners in the final 150 yards, and a horse travelling smoothly in mid-division sweeps through on the outside of the tired leaders; this shape rewards those with a strong cruising speed and an ability to quicken off a fast tempo.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Hold-Up Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners panic early, set an overly frantic pace, and collapse dramatically leaving a late-finishing hold-up type to scoop the race.
scenarios.body: Earth Shot, mapped here as a hold-up runner though a natural prominent racer, benefits only if the pace genuinely collapses far enough for a horse coming from off it to pick them all off; this is the least likely shape given no true hold-up specialists are in the field.

watchPoints.text: Tattycoram and Johanna Walsh both want the lead — watch the first furlong closely as a contested, aggressive battle between these two could either produce a contested lead that burns both out or a clear separation that decides the tactical shape of the entire race.

Legacy Link's 63-day layoff is the longest in the field; watch whether William Buick lets her stride forward naturally in the early stages or whether rust causes her to be sluggish out of the gates, which would fundamentally alter her race position and chance.

Sparan Nua runs just 14 days after her last start, and if that quick turnaround leaves her short of peak freshness, Rossa Ryan may find her unable to sustain a prominent position in the straight when the strong gallop bites hard.

Prominent congestion involving Kalpana, Minnie Hauk, Inis Mor, and Sparan Nua means the 2f-3f-out section could produce significant traffic problems on the turn into York's straight — watch for horses becoming briefly stopped or forced widest of all on the run to the home turn.

Earth Shot's natural preference for racing close to the pace means her actual finishing position will depend heavily on whether she can avoid being shuffled back by the front-running scramble early — if she loses contact with the pace in the first half mile, her chance diminishes sharply.

races.name: British Ebf & Sir Henry Cecil Galtres Stakes (Listed Race) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Ashariba
runners_data.note: Won twice at 10f on good/soft including a Listed race; steps back up in trip to 1m4f where her one good-ground run at the trip produced a win — David Menuisier's runner comes here after 55 days off and will push for prominent position from the outset.|

runners_data.name: Club Class
runners_data.note: Six places from six runs on comparable ground and a regular at 1m4f-1m5f trips; wears a tongue-pin and James Fanshawe sends her in good form (6/24 over 14 days) but she remains elusive to win, and the congested prominent zone makes it harder still.|

runners_data.name: Merveilleux Lapin
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up runner with three placings from six on good ground; Callum Rodriguez takes the ride for Owen Burrows and this mare has shown she stays 1m4f well — her patient style fits a scenario where the front-runners exhaust each other.|

runners_data.name: Morrophore
runners_data.note: The highest-rated older horse in the field at OR 105 with three wins including two on good going at around a mile; Ryan Moore takes over after a 215-day absence and her stamina for 1m4f is unexposed — but the class edge is undeniable if fit.|

runners_data.name: Perfect Your Craft
runners_data.note: Won over 1m4f on good going at Leopardstown and placed at the trip here at York last time; wears a hood and Pat Twomey sends him across from Ireland — he will push for the prominent position he needs but faces a crowded berth.|

runners_data.name: Rhapsody
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse with a win and three places on good ground; Tom Marquand has ridden her twice and William Haggas sends her in form (6/37 over 14 days) — she is ideally suited by a genuinely run race over this trip where she can close from off the pace.|

runners_data.name: Ryka
runners_data.note: Won back-to-back over 1m4f (both on ground softer than today) and has form on good going at the trip; David O'Meara's filly returns after a 111-day break which is the longest absence among the field and represents the main fitness query.|

runners_data.name: A La Prochaine
runners_data.note: A Ralph Beckett three-year-old with a single win over 1m but placed twice at 1m4f on good ground; James Doyle, who rode her last time, will try to secure a handy prominent position in a competitive older-horse field — the step into Listed company from three-year-old maiden form is her key test.|

runners_data.name: Capichera
runners_data.note: Won over 1m at Sandown on good ground last month; by nature a prominent racer but the density of horses wanting that position in this field means she is likely to find herself racing in a deeper midfield than suits her best, which tempers her chance.|

runners_data.name: K Sarra
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has been tried in blinkers; a hold-up type with only one win and some inconsistent form figures recently (7th, 8th at 1m4f) — Ralph Beckett also runs A La Prochaine, and the 33-day turnaround at 1m4f on good ground is straightforward enough.|

runners_data.name: Prizeland
runners_data.note: One of only two confirmed front-runners alongside Vauntingly; Oisin Murphy's mount has won over 1m4f-1m5f on good and soft and will take them on from the front — at OR 94 she is the lowest-rated horse attempting to lead, and whether she can sustain it against Vauntingly is the key tactical question.|

runners_data.name: Summerson
runners_data.note: Won over 1m4f on good ground at Haydock last time and has been placed in all three career starts; wears a hood and Roger Varian sends her in after just 23 days — her unbeaten sequence at this trip and this going makes her unexposed profile intriguing, though she is a first-time Listed runner.|

runners_data.name: Sunshine Star
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent-racing type by inclination for the Gosdens, she ran second over 1m4f on good ground at Newmarket last time; however, the crowded prominent sector means she will almost certainly find herself in a deeper position than she prefers, and STYLE_FIT concerns apply.|

runners_data.name: Vauntingly
runners_data.note: The other confirmed front-runner and arguably the one with the stronger credentials to lead: Dylan Browne McMonagle has ridden her to four consecutive places on good ground, including a win at 1m4f — she will fight for the lead with Prizeland from the off and is the horse most likely to establish herself at the front.|

runners_data.name: Without Prejudice
runners_data.note: Won on her only start over 1m on good ground at Newmarket for the Gosdens with William Buick riding; lightly raced (just one run) and moving straight into Listed company is a significant jump — the talent may be there but the absence of evidence beyond a single maiden win demands caution.|

races.paceDynamic: Vauntingly and Prizeland are the two confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset, creating a genuine, honest pace on good ground over 1m4f at York — neither is a natural leader who will simply gift the others a soft early gallop. With six of fifteen runners wanting a prominent position, there will be early jostling and crowding behind the two pacemakers, creating meaningful traffic risks two to three furlongs out as the field concertinas entering the straight. Capichera and Sunshine Star are genuine prominent-racing types by nature but are mapped to midfield here simply because Vauntingly, Prizeland, Morrophore, Club Class, Perfect Your Craft, A La Prochaine, and Ryka will all be fighting for the limited premium spots ahead of them — Vauntingly and Prizeland hold the best draw and pace credentials to secure the front two, with Morrophore and Club Class the most likely to anchor the prominent berths behind. The contested lead on good ground over this staying trip moderately favours hold-up and late-running profiles who can track the pace without fighting for position, but the congestion risk means a horse with tactical ease sitting just off the pace — Morrophore, Rhapsody, or A La Prochaine — could prove ideally placed if the scramble for position burns the prominent horses out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Vauntingly and Prizeland push each other along at a genuine clip, burning off those jammed in behind them.
scenarios.body: The honest gallop set by the two front-runners stretches the field early and leaves prominent horses exposed by the two-furlong pole, bringing the hold-up runners into play late; Rhapsody and Merveilleux Lapin, both patient hold-up types with strong form on good ground, are ideally suited to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Quickens
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest but not brutal, leaving one prominent runner with reserves to quicken off the final bend.
scenarios.body: A horse who tracks the early leaders in the first three or four without expending energy in the positional battle emerges with something left when the front two tire; Morrophore, a multiple winner at around this trip on good ground with Ryan Moore in the saddle, is the archetype for this shape, as is A La Prochaine from a slightly deeper prominent spot.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If either Vauntingly or Prizeland seizes a clear early lead and the field is complacent, allowing a comfortable front-running display.
scenarios.body: One of the two leaders — most likely Vauntingly given four consecutive placed efforts on good ground and Dylan Browne McMonagle's positive riding style — dictates an even tempo, keeps enough in reserve, and simply refuses to be caught in the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp Field
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fierce enough to compromise the whole front pack and leave the race wide open entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With Sunshine Star and Capichera both unable to secure their natural prominent position and forced to race in midfield, true hold-up runners without redistribution concerns — Rhapsody, Merveilleux Lapin, K Sarra — are best placed to capitalise on a chaotic finish; Without Prejudice, lightly raced but highly touted, could also emerge if connections have readied her for a big effort.

watchPoints.text: Vauntingly and Prizeland will fight for the lead from flag fall — watch for an early duel that sets a searching pace and compromises both of them before the straight, which could open the door for a prominent tracker.

The prominent berth is dangerously overcrowded: Morrophore, Club Class, Perfect Your Craft, A La Prochaine, Ryka, Sunshine Star, and Capichera all want a forward position — horses drawn widest or slowest away risk being shuffled back and losing significant ground two furlongs in.

Sunshine Star and Capichera are both natural prominent racers who are likely to find themselves in unnatural midfield positions given the field's pace profile — do not read their mapped position as their genuine running style when assessing how the race shapes up.

Morrophore returns from a 215-day absence for the Gosdens with Ryan Moore; without a public trial run, how she handles race-fitness at a stiff 1m4f on good ground is the key unknown — watch for signs of rustiness in the market and at the start.

Without Prejudice steps from a single maiden win straight into Listed company with William Buick; lightly raced horses for Gosden/Buick can arrive here ready to win, but the absence of any form lines beyond one run means any market drift is a significant signal.

races.name: Mews Hotel Ossett Ebf Stallions Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Big Cigar
runners_data.note: Won twice including at 7f on Good ground, Ethan Tindall (5lb claim) partnership with Fahey is live; races prominently and the step to 7f suits — solid each-way profile in this shape.|

runners_data.name: Revels
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke in-form (T14: 6/28), Sam James aboard; confirmed front-runner who has won twice at 7f on Good, goes well on this surface — the horse most likely to dominate the early pace battle.|

runners_data.name: Shadow King
runners_data.note: Hannon runner with a hood (blinkers), capable of winning on Good ground at 7f but last run was a disappointing 9th; prominent racer who needs to recapture his best after that York flop.|

runners_data.name: Perfect Nation
runners_data.note: Boughey's progressive filly has won back-to-back and goes well on Good — Billy Loughnane takes the ride and she is a confirmed front-runner, though the presence of Revels and Weleyff makes unopposed lead unlikely.|

runners_data.name: Soldier Of The Sea
runners_data.note: Only two runs but both placings on Good ground and won at 6f; steps up to 7f for the first time, prominent runner for William Knight who has had no runners in the last 14 days — watch the market.|

runners_data.name: Weleyff
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell in excellent form (T14: 9/24), Oisin Orr takes the ride; two wins from two at 7f on Good, confirmed front-runner who will press for the lead and is well-suited by this trip and going.|

runners_data.name: Rising Tiger
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's mount for Andrew Balding; placed in all three starts and handles 7f on Good well, prominent racer who should travel smoothly — needs luck in a congested 22-runner field.|

runners_data.name: My A'Ali Baba
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne on a genuine hold-up type who ran only 8 days ago; mixed form over 7f-8f, best efforts have come on Soft, so the Good ground here may not fully play to her strengths.|

runners_data.name: Bymiddaytomorrow
runners_data.note: Two wins from his last two starts at 7f on Good ground under Tom Marquand for Ed Walker — prominent racer stepping forward in trip after impressive progression, strong profile for the dominant race shape.|

runners_data.name: The Ginger Kid
runners_data.note: Kieran Shoemark rides this hold-up type for Ed Walker; very consistent at 7f on Good (5/5 sim-going), placed in all recent outings — needs a clean run through a packed field but the style suits a strong pace.|

runners_data.name: Mirzimaan
runners_data.note: William Buick on a Boughey hold-up type who won at 6f on Good and was placed at 7f on Standard — stepping up in trip and competition, but Buick's positional awareness could be crucial in traffic.|

runners_data.name: Telegraphic
runners_data.note: Callum Shepherd on a Charlie Johnston horse who has won at 7f on Good and is 3/3 on similar ground; races prominently and the form progression is consistent — viable each-way claim in this field.|

runners_data.name: Caeruleus
runners_data.note: David Egan on a hold-up type for John Butler; only one run on Good going in five starts, which is a notable concern — may prefer a bit of cut and is exposed here against stronger rivals.|

runners_data.name: Mia Fantasia
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's prominent racer won at 7f on Good ground and placed twice at this trip — Marco Ghiani in the saddle; a last-run 6th at York over this course and distance slightly tempers enthusiasm.|

runners_data.name: Roosike
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes' runner won most recently at 7f on Standard, but only one run on Good going in three starts; a confirmed front-runner who will try to get cover on the lead, though outpaced by Revels and Perfect Nation early.|

runners_data.name: Koodini
runners_data.note: Wears a hood (p), recent 7f winner on Good ground for Hugo Palmer, Aiden Brookes rides; a genuine hold-up type whose best form has come when travelling smoothly into a race — needs clear air in a big field.|

runners_data.name: High Hazard
runners_data.note: Also wears a hood (p) for Hugo Palmer, Cam Hardie up; disappointing last run (16th) at 7f on Good is a red flag, and the form profile over 7f-8f is limited — difficult to fancy at current weights.|

runners_data.name: Regal Tiger
runners_data.note: Andrew Mullen on a Hugo Palmer horse with three runs all resulting in placed efforts; handles Good ground over shorter trips — steps up to 7f for the first time and prominent position will be required.|

runners_data.name: Theheatison
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes the ride for Nick Scholfield; one win on Firm, minor form on Good — last run was a third over 7f on Good which is encouraging but the handicapper has him well assessed here.|

runners_data.name: High Calibre
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen on a Richard Hannon hold-up type; placed in a 8f handicap on Good most recently — handles going well but limited profile in this company and yet to show a win.|

runners_data.name: Rbflying
runners_data.note: Veteran of Tim Easterby's yard, Duran Fentiman rides; in his last five runs on Good ground he has never finished better than third — his natural instinct is to come from off the pace but in this 22-runner cavalry charge he is unlikely to find his preferred position at the rear.|

runners_data.name: Fasthope
runners_data.note: A recent 6f winner on Good ground for Brian Ellison is his best recent form, though absent 44 days; a genuine closer by inclination who is being squeezed into a midfield berth by the sheer volume of hold-up types in this field, which means he won't get the clean run his style demands.|

races.paceDynamic: Revels, Perfect Nation, and Weleyff are all confirmed front-runners in a 22-runner field, and with Roosike also likely to push forward from a prominent position, this race will be run at a strong, unrelenting gallop from the break over York's flat 7f. The early battle for supremacy between these pace horses will ensure sectionals are genuine throughout, stretching the field and placing a premium on stamina and the ability to sustain effort into the final two furlongs. Nine of the 22 runners want a prominent position, creating significant congestion and traffic risk between the 2f and 3f poles, which will be a serious concern for horses drawn wide or caught in the pack. Fasthope and Rbflying are true hold-up types who have been mapped to midfield simply because the race has more rear-dwellers than the map can accommodate at the back — of the front-runners, Revels and Perfect Nation, with their strong recent records at this trip and going, are most likely to actually dominate the early stages. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or at least in the first half of the field without burning resources, and who possess genuine 7f stamina — pure speed merchants and true closers face a compressed finishing window with a strong pace to aim at, but the chaotic early stages and traffic risks in the pack mean that position and luck in running matter enormously.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Revels, Perfect Nation, and Weleyff fight for supremacy and set a true end-to-end gallop, the race becomes a genuine stamina test.
scenarios.body: The leaders will have burned significant energy by halfway, meaning horses who race prominently without over-committing early — just off the pace — will be perfectly placed to pick off the tiring leaders in the final furlong; York's flat 7f rewards those who travel smoothly through the race. Bymiddaytomorrow, Big Cigar, and Telegraphic, all of whom have winning form at this trip on Good ground and can take up a prominent position without fighting for the lead, are ideally profiled for this outcome.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates Wire
scenarios.trigger: If one of the confirmed leaders — most likely Revels or Perfect Nation — gets a clear rail run and is not severely pressured into an unsustainable tempo.
scenarios.body: With a large field and multiple early pace horses, it is possible that one bold front-runner establishes a comfortable lead while the others cancel each other out, allowing the leader to dictate a controlled gallop and sprint clear; Revels, who has won twice at 7f on Good ground and is trained by the in-form K.R. Burke, is best placed to exploit this shape. Perfect Nation's recent back-to-back wins and ability to lead from the front also make her a primary beneficiary if the pace proves more moderate than the pace map suggests.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Comes Through Traffic
scenarios.trigger: If the early scramble for prominent positions creates traffic chaos between the 2f and 3f markers, and horses in the middle of the pack find a clear run.
scenarios.body: Mirzimaan, The Ginger Kid, and Caeruleus, all of whom are genuine hold-up or midfield types with proven form at 7f on Good ground, could benefit if the race falls apart for the prominent runners in a congested final quarter-mile; the key is a clean passage through the pack, which with 22 runners is far from guaranteed. Rising Tiger, who has been placed in all three starts and is ridden by Oisin Murphy, possesses the class to make a late challenge if produced with a clear run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail, Chaos Plays Out
scenarios.trigger: If the genuine hold-up horses — including Rbflying and Fasthope, who are displaced from their natural position — are caught in traffic and the race produces a messy, compressed finish.
scenarios.body: Because Rbflying and Fasthope are true rear-dwellers racing out of role in a deeply congested field, their chances of delivering a telling late run are materially reduced; any scenario that depends on them producing their best hold-up effort is undermined by the reality that they will not secure their natural berth. The beneficiaries of this shape would most likely be horses in the middle-to-rear of the field who find a gap late — Koodini, a recent 7f winner on Good ground, wears a hood and could respond if produced at the right moment, but this is the lowest-probability shape in the race.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion is extreme — 9 of 22 runners target the same first-quarter-mile position; horses drawn high or wide (particularly double-figure stalls) face a near-impossible task getting to the rail and may be shuffled back sharply, costing several lengths before the race truly begins.

Revels, Perfect Nation, and Weleyff will almost certainly clash for supremacy in the first two furlongs — if none concede the lead early, sectionals could be explosive and set up a significantly shorter race from halfway, which could fatally undermine all three leaders' winning chances.

Traffic danger between the 2f and 3f poles is the single biggest tactical hazard in this race: horses like Mirzimaan, The Ginger Kid, and Koodini must find clear passage through a densely packed field or face being bottled up behind stopping rivals at the worst possible moment.

Rbflying and Fasthope, true hold-up types forced into midfield by the race map, are at serious risk of being caught in the worst of the traffic with no ability to switch wide or produce their customary late run — discount them in any shape that requires a genuine late finish.

Bymiddaytomorrow's back-to-back wins both came at 7f on Good ground and were achieved in progressive handicap fashion — any market confidence for Tom Marquand's mount should be noted as a possible market indicator of the dominant race shape.

races.name: British Ebf Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Bellarchi
runners_data.note: Proven hold-up performer who has won three of her last five on Good ground including twice at 7f; trainer Tuer fires at 1/9 over 14 days and this is exactly the strong-gallop 7f race her style is built for; 44 days off is worth monitoring but form is live.

runners_data.name: Royal Velvet
runners_data.note: All five of her career runs in similar going have produced a placed or winning effort — an extraordinary record — and she drops back to 7f where she has won twice; hold-up style perfectly suited to a hot pace; Conor Whiteley's 5lb claim adds interest.

runners_data.name: Mubasimah
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Balding who has done most of her racing at 8f and showed a worrying drop in form recently; likely to fight for the lead against Caim, Machadadorp and others which risks burning out; trainer T14 of 6/49 is moderate.

runners_data.name: Lam Yai
runners_data.note: 299 days off the track is a significant concern for a three-year-old, and her best form has come at 5-6f on soft; stepping up to 7f on Good ground first time back makes this a speculative assignment despite Burke's ability to train fit horses.

runners_data.name: Just Call Me Angel
runners_data.note: Two smart wins at 8f on Good ground earlier in the season but has gone backward sharply since (7th, 11th, 12th) and wears a hood; hold-up profile suits the likely pace but the sharp form dip cannot be ignored.

runners_data.name: Tryst
runners_data.note: Won his last two races at 7f on Good ground and is progressing as a three-year-old; Boughey sends horses out fit and Loughnane is in fine form; a genuine hold-up type who could thrive if the pace serves him up a clear run in the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Carnival Of Light
runners_data.note: Won twice at 7f on Tapeta so the turf Good is an untested angle; prominent style should get a handy position in this field but the going question is real and sim-going record shows 0W0P in comparable conditions.

runners_data.name: Bella Lyra
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has placed at 7f on Soft and Standard surfaces; 75 days off and an 8f last run raises a query about peak condition, but Richard Hughes trains her well and Finley Marsh rode her last time for a placed effort.

runners_data.name: Oolong Poobong
runners_data.note: Won at 7f on Good ground and has hit the frame at that trip before; wore a tongue tie and was below par last time over 8f but reverts to the 7f trip that suits; Bethell yard is in top form (T14: 9/24) and Oisin Orr is a smart booking.

runners_data.name: Figjam
runners_data.note: Six runs all at 6-7f on Good ground without a win and a current form string reading 746467 does not inspire confidence; hold-up runner who is more likely to be a market foil than a serious challenger unless something dramatically changes.

runners_data.name: Beaujolais Nouveau
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who likes to race from off the pace — his natural role will be compromised in this traffic-heavy field as he is mapped to a midfield position he does not naturally occupy; his 6f best form is a further concern over 7f here; STYLE_FIT 0.93 tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Caim
runners_data.note: Front-runner who won over 8f on Soft and showed pace at 7f on Soft earlier in the season; 86 days off is a worry on return to Good ground and a contested lead against Mubasimah and Machadadorp could unravel his chance quickly.

runners_data.name: Albaydaa
runners_data.note: Placed four of five career starts at 7f on Good including two wins; Haggas and Marquand is a powerful combination and she should get a prominent position without necessarily leading; consistent profile that suits a pressured pace race.

runners_data.name: Perfect Part
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer who is placed out of her natural position in this field; sim-going record of 11/15 without a win speaks for itself, and the 5lb apprentice makes this a tough ask in a competitive handicap; STYLE_FIT 0.92.

runners_data.name: Machadadorp
runners_data.note: Won back-to-back 7f Good ground races and carries Oisin Murphy — a formidable booking — for the in-form Balding team; one of the most likely horses to secure a clean lead position if Mubasimah and Caim take each other on; strong contender if the speed fight plays out favourably.

runners_data.name: Starlight Lass
runners_data.note: Won her last two races including a 7f Soft effort and has only three career runs, meaning she is lightly raced and progressing; Gosden yard with Saffie Osborne suggests confidence, and a front-running style at 7f on Good could see her lead a weakened field home.

runners_data.name: Starfinch
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner whose only Good ground win came at 6f on Tapeta; recent form includes a 3rd at 7f on Good and a 9th at 6f, suggesting inconsistency; George Wood is a capable claimer but this looks a very tough heat.

runners_data.name: Secret History
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has won at 7f on Good ground and carries a hood; Ed Walker sends horses out tuned up and her sim-going record of 6/7 placed is solid; dropping in class from some recent efforts and should get a handy pitch.

runners_data.name: Cotai Belle
runners_data.note: Remarkably consistent placed horse — four seconds in her last four starts at 6f — but yet to win on Good ground and the step up to 7f is untested; Cam Hardie should get her a handy position, and her consistency in defeat makes her a place contender.

runners_data.name: Woohoo
runners_data.note: Five consecutive second places on Good ground below 7f and a genuine hold-up profile that is likely to be shuffled into midfield rather than her preferred backmarking role in this 21-runner field; STYLE_FIT 0.92 and the unfamiliar 7f trip are both headwinds.

runners_data.name: Zooella
runners_data.note: Front-runner who won her last two over 6f but has limited Going Good form over the distance; Silvestre De Sousa is a smart jockey to have on a pace-setter, but with four other leaders to fight, her chance depends on controlling the race rather than racing in it.

races.paceDynamic: Mubasimah, Caim, Machadadorp, Starlight Lass, and Zooella all carry genuine front-running profiles, meaning this seven-furlong York contest will be contested at a strong, unrelenting gallop from the outset with no shortage of horses bidding to control proceedings — the pace-battle itself becomes a race within the race. With five leaders fighting for the front, those that press hardest early will likely exhaust themselves and their rivals, stretching the field and burning off tactical speed before the final two furlongs. The field also contains more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Beaujolais Nouveau, Perfect Part, and Woohoo are genuine closers but are likely to find themselves shuffled into a midfield position rather than their preferred backmarking spot, somewhat blunting their effectiveness. This race shape overwhelmingly favours the patient hold-up runner with proven stamina for the trip and the ability to pick up a strong gallop in the final furlong, making genuine late-finishing profiles and horses who have won at 7f+ on Good ground the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the five-way pace battle burns out the leaders turning for home, leaving genuine hold-up horses to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: The contested early fractions drain the pace contingent before the final two furlongs, creating a wall of tired horses for closers to reel in. Horses with proven finishing kicks on Good ground at 7f who can be produced with one late run are best placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Nails It
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters slots into second or third early and avoids the worst of the speed duel before kicking clear.
scenarios.body: A horse that earns a comfortable prominent position without leading outright avoids the brunt of the speed battle and holds enough in reserve to power home. Albaydaa, Oolong Poobong, or Carnival Of Light could be the beneficiary if they negotiate traffic from a handy pitch.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On Gamely
scenarios.trigger: If one pace-setter breaks cleanly, dictates on its own terms, and the field never fully coalesces to mount a coordinated challenge.
scenarios.body: With five horses vying for the lead, one clean break — most likely Machadadorp or Starlight Lass given their recent form at this trip — could see them settle into an uncontested rhythm slightly off the true pace and prove harder to peg back. Good ground suits both, and a messy midfield behind them would reduce the threat from closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Scramble Produces Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is frantic but the closers are compromised by traffic, and a midfield horse threads through between the two groups.
scenarios.body: A large 21-runner field creates significant positional chaos, and a horse sitting seventh or eighth with a smart jockey finding a seam at the two-furlong pole could emerge from the wreckage. Bella Lyra or Cotai Belle, both placed types who travel prominently without leading, fit the profile if the gaps materialise.

watchPoints.text: Mubasimah, Caim, and Machadadorp are all confirmed front-runners — watch for a bitter five-way pace battle from the off that could compromise all of them and dramatically accelerate the finish.
Machadadorp carries Oisin Murphy and has won his last two 7f Good ground starts; if he breaks cleanly and avoids the worst of the speed duel, he is the most dangerous front-runner in the field.

Royal Velvet has a remarkable record in similar going (15 from 15 placed runs) and holds-up for a late run — watch for her to be delivered wide in the final furlong if a clear run inside is blocked in a 21-runner field.
Starlight Lass is lightly raced (only three career runs) and unexposed — a horse progressing this sharply from the Gosden yard with a front-running style at 7f could easily outrun a big price.

Beaujolais Nouveau, Perfect Part, and Woohoo are all genuine closers likely to be racing out of role in the midfield — monitor whether they can extricate themselves in the straight, as their finishing kicks will be diluted if they cannot settle in their natural position.
